sources.title: Parliament of Uganda: History of Parliament
sources.note: Colonial council membership, constitutional changes, military interruption and 1995 constitution. Institutional narrative, not a complete political history.

sources.title: Uganda Independence Order in Council, 1962
sources.note: Explanatory note identifies 9 October 1962; constitution and schedules distinguish kingdoms and central institutions.

sources.title: The African Archives: The Uganda Agreement of 1900
sources.note: Transcribed agreement: British overrule, kingdom administration, taxation and land, concluded at Mengo in English and Luganda.

sources.title: Makerere University: History
sources.note: Institutional history: 1922 technical school, 14 day students, carpentry/building/mechanics; subsequent medical, agricultural and teaching courses.

sources.title: John Tosh: Lango Agriculture during the early Colonial Period
sources.note: Journal of African History 19 (1978), abstract: sesame trade and household labour constraints; shift towards cotton in early 1920s.

sources.title: Cambridge University Library: Uganda Co. Ltd. Part of cotton ginnery
sources.note: Photograph catalogue describes Ugandan workers operating seed-separating machines. Exact exposure date not given on viewed landing page; no invented date.

sources.title: Kirk Arden Hoppe: Lords of the fly
sources.note: Africa article: forced depopulations, clearing, resettlement and land alienation, 1906 to 1962; African responses and competing colonial agendas.

sources.title: Daniel R. Headrick: Sleeping Sickness Epidemics and Colonial Responses in East and Central Africa, 1900 to 1940
sources.note: British Environmental Approach section: lakeshore removals, fishing and firewood restrictions; avoid contested mortality totals and historical treatments as advice.

sources.title: Emma Wild-Wood and George Mpanga: Kivebulaya’s Published Articles
sources.note: British Academy 2021, pages 93 to 96; abstract gives Ebifa mu Buganda, translation, January 1907 foundation, and articles on colonial borders.

sources.title: SCOLMA: African Research and Documentation 136
sources.note: Discussion of Ugandan missionary archives: Luganda periodicals, poems, proverbs, social affairs; surviving copies at Makerere and Rubaga.

sources.title: UNESCO: Barkcloth making in Uganda
sources.note: Living Baganda practice inscribed in 2008: wet-season mutuba bark, mallets, sheds, ceremonial and household uses. Do not project every modern detail to a specific earlier century.

sources.title: Makerere University: The Kiira Electric Vehicle, Proudly Makererean
sources.note: 2 November 2011 report of campus test drive on 1 November: two-seat prototype, aluminium-alloy chassis. Avoid treating target specifications as measured performance.

sources.title: UNICEF: Sato Pans transforming health in Kamuli District
sources.note: 10 January 2024, named households and mason, closing flap, washable floors, privacy and handwashing; individual examples, not nationwide uniform access.

sources.title: UNICEF: It’s all about the water
sources.note: 25 March 2022: Nyumazi solar water system and latrine blocks, Unaa kitchen supply, Amelo community management.

sources.title: UNESCO: Bigwala, gourd trumpet music and dance
sources.note: 2012 urgent safeguarding inscription; five or more single-note trumpets, ensemble melody, social occasions and historical songs. Do not use changing bearer counts as present-day census.

sources.title: African Books Collective: The Defence of Lawino
sources.note: Fountain Publishers title description and author biography: Acholi Wer pa Lawino published 1969, English Song of Lawino in 1966; literary family argument, not ethnographic census.

sources.title: WorldCat: Wer pa Lawino, 1969 edition
sources.note: Catalogue verifies original Acholi title and East African Publishing House, Nairobi, 1969.

sources.title: UK National Archives: Colonial administration records guidance
sources.note: Kenya background: 1895 protectorate, 1920 colony, coastal protectorate distinction.

sources.title: Kenya Railways: History
sources.note: Nairobi reached in 1899 and Kisumu in 1901; Indian and African workers. Retain factual dates without repeating derogatory colonial vocabulary or progress rhetoric.

sources.title: Smithsonian: Tin identity pass holder, kipande
sources.note: 1920s case contained employment paper dated 1925, collected in 1986 and accessioned 1998; manufacture and collection dates distinguished.

sources.title: Colonial Urbanization and Urban Management in Kenya
sources.note: African Urban Spaces in Historical Perspective (2005), pages 73 to 97, summary: racial land/housing restrictions, bachelor accommodation and African/Asian responses.

sources.title: The Airlift Generation, Economic Aspiration, and Secondary School Education in Kenya, 1940 to 1960
sources.note: Historical background and Maseno/Alliance sections supply earlier 1910, 1926 and 1928 evidence; do not transfer postwar pupil figures into 1920s.

sources.title: Resurrecting the African Independent Pentecostal Church
sources.note: Background on KISA in 1930s: elected committees, donated land and community fundraising.

sources.title: Cambridge Centre for Christianity Worldwide: Muigwithania
sources.note: Catalogue MUI, 1928 to 1929 newspaper issues in Kikuyu with contemporary English translations; correspondence and colonial scrutiny.

sources.title: WorldCat: Muigwithania and associated papers, 1928 to 1929
sources.note: Title translation given as Reconciler, Unifier or Newsbearer; original title spelling retained.

sources.title: Central Bank of Kenya: Currency History
sources.note: Florin to shilling transition; first national notes used Banki Kuu ya Kenya/Central Bank of Kenya. Avoid introductory claim that all African economies used only barter.

sources.title: Presidential Library and Museum: Independence comes
sources.note: 12 December 1963 independence and December 1964 republic; celebratory institutional narrative used for chronology only.

sources.title: Parliament of Kenya: History fact sheet
sources.note: 1963 and 1964 constitutional phases; 2010 constitution restored a bicameral parliament.

sources.title: Green Belt Movement: History
sources.note: Organization’s own account of 1977 foundation, women’s firewood/water/food concerns and community education.

sources.title: Nobel Prize: The Nobel Peace Prize 2004, press release
sources.note: Official award explanation: Maathai, environmental conservation, democracy and peace.

sources.title: Safaricom: How M-PESA was created
sources.note: 28 February 2025 retrospective: trial users repurposed loan-payment system for transfers; 2007 launch and named rollout leader. Company perspective attributed.

sources.title: Safaricom Annual Report 2021: Our business model
sources.note: Describes cash deposits, phone account, PIN-secured messages and redemption; no claim Kenya alone invented mobile money.

sources.title: UNICEF: Clean Toilets, Brighter Futures, schools in Kitui
sources.note: 17 November 2025, St. Marks Makutano school, accessible cubicles, health club and soap-making; local reported outcomes, not a causal nationwide evaluation.

sources.title: UNESCO: Traditions and practices associated with the Kayas
sources.note: Mijikenda living practices, councils, rites and resource management. Avoid confusing intangible heritage with separate forest World Heritage inscription.

sources.title: United Nations: Mandates and proposed trusteeship agreements, A/70
sources.note: Reproduces British mandate for Tanganyika confirmed in 1922; distinguishes mandate from later trusteeship.

sources.title: Martin Sturmer: The Media History of Tanzania
sources.note: Printed pages 51 to 52: Mambo Leo title, translation, 1923 launch, topics, pen friendships, missing-person notices and circulation.

sources.title: Somo M. L. Seimu and Marco Zoppi: The Influence of Settlers’ Community in Shaping the Colonial Agricultural Marketing Policies in Tanzania
sources.note: African Economic History 49(2), 2021, pages 53 to 76; author-deposited abstract: Kilimanjaro growers, settler opposition and 1932/1937 ordinances.

sources.title: Nicholas Westcott: The East African Sisal Industry, 1929 to 1949
sources.note: Journal of African History, 1984; abstract: rapid expansion and Depression-era marketing problems.

sources.title: Sascha Klocke: Skill, Race, and Income Inequality in the Wage Sector in British Tanganyika
sources.note: Research abstract: educational provision, skilled labour shortages, wage inequality, approximately 1920 to 1960.

sources.title: Jonathan M. Jackson: Coercion and Dissent in Ulanga, Tanganyika
sources.note: 2022 study; Ulanga District section on river livelihoods; policy discussion distinguishes 1930s proposals from concentration beginning in 1939.

sources.title: Tanganyika Constitution Order in Council, 1961
sources.note: Primary constitutional instrument; independence on 9 December 1961.

sources.title: United Republic of Tanzania: Report to the UN Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights
sources.note: 2011 state report, introductory constitutional history: independence, republic, 26 April 1964 union, two governments.

sources.title: Indiana University: Azimio la Arusha, 1967 pamphlet
sources.note: Swahili catalogue title of TANU Information Department pamphlet, item 8074.

sources.title: Agency and the Arusha Declaration: Nyerere, NUTA, and Political Discourse in Tanzania, 1966 to 1967
sources.note: Journal of African History, 2023; title translation, socialism, nationalization and political agency.

sources.title: Sebastian Edwards: The Arusha Declaration, Foreign Aid, and the Crisis of 1979
sources.note: Toxic Aid, Oxford University Press, chapter abstract explicitly identifies forced movement of peasants to villages.

sources.title: UNESCO: Integrated Community-Based Adult Education in Tanzania
sources.note: 2017 programme account: 1993 inception, literacy circles, sewing-machine loan example, practical bookkeeping.

sources.title: Tanzania-Zambia Railway Authority: Our History
sources.note: Official project chronology, route, construction, 14 July 1976 full operations; separate engineering facts from celebratory rhetoric.

sources.title: UNICEF: WASH in schools, Bahati School
sources.note: 27 May 2017, named school in Temeke, sanitation facilities and health teacher/student routines.

sources.title: Nobel Prize: Abdulrazak Gurnah, Facts
sources.note: 2021 literature award, Zanzibar childhood, persecution and refugee experience; fiction is not used as a census of everyday practices.

sources.title: Republic of South Sudan: Common core document, 2020
sources.note: UN-hosted state report, paragraphs 6 to 7: Anglo-Egyptian rule, independence in 1956, civil wars and 2005 peace agreement.

sources.title: United Nations: South Sudan
sources.note: Secession on 9 July 2011 following referendum, UN membership on 14 July.

sources.title: United Nations: Background to a crisis in Sudan
sources.note: 1 May 2023: 2019 transition, October 2021 coup and April 2023 fighting.

sources.title: World Bank: The World Bank and the Gezira Scheme in the Sudan
sources.note: 30 June 2010 report, executive summary and historical section: 1925 inauguration after Sennar Dam, government/tenant/company relations.

sources.title: World Bank: Description of existing irrigation schemes, Annex III
sources.note: Annex III, paragraphs 1 to 5: clay soils, Sennar Dam, canals, cotton, dura and lubia. Historical report figures are not current statistics.

sources.title: Royal College of Physicians: The Kitchener School of Medicine
sources.note: 20 October 2017, Sarah Gillam: 1924 opening, hospital training, 1928 graduates, Ali Bedri and later University of Khartoum.

sources.title: Heather Bell: Midwifery Training and Female Circumcision in the Inter-War Anglo-Egyptian Sudan
sources.note: Journal of African History, 1998; abstract and study of Omdurman Midwifery Training School opened in 1921.

sources.title: Ahfad University for Women: About AUW
sources.note: Institutional chronology from 1907 girls’ school through 1966 college and 1995 university; rural extension from 1973 and requirement in 1978.

sources.title: WorldCat: موسم الهجرة الى الشمال
sources.note: Arabic title as catalogued, including الى spelling, 1997 Beirut edition; original publication year comes from NYRB.

sources.title: New York Review Books: Season of Migration to the North
sources.note: Publisher identifies Tayeb Salih’s 1966 novel and English title; only title sampled, no passage used to generalize customs.

sources.title: UNDP: Women leading crisis recovery and building resilience
sources.note: 2025 account of women-led community kitchens in Sudan, meals and relationships between displaced and host communities.

sources.title: UNICEF Sudan: 2025 humanitarian situation reports
sources.note: End-of-year account of emergency services, health facilities and mobile teams; describes a dated response during war, not current front lines.

sources.title: U.S. Office of the Historian: Founding of Liberia, 1847
sources.note: Historical overview of American Colonization Society, settlement and independent republic; Liberia was not a U.S. government colony.

sources.title: Library of Congress: From Colony to Independence, Mid-19th Century Maps of Liberia
sources.note: Tim St. Onge, 9 August 2017; McClellan’s 1850 map, depth soundings, settlements and customs revenue. Direct fetch denied, indexed official text checked.

sources.title: Liberia Legal Information Institute: Constitution of 1847
sources.note: Transcription of convention declaration and constitution; exact brief English phrase from preamble, PDF page 4.

sources.title: Library of Congress: History of Liberia, a time line
sources.note: Indexed official timeline checked: 1904 indirect government, 1946 franchise extension, 1980 coup and 1986 constitution. Do not use its problematic 1989 claim that Doe was toppled that year.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Wunkirmian or wakemia feasting spoon
sources.note: Dan artist, nineteenth to mid-twentieth century; wooden ladle, hospitality and responsibilities of wunkirle; Liberia/Côte d’Ivoire cultural context.

sources.title: Nobel Prize: Leymah Gbowee, biographical
sources.note: Gbowee’s biography: interfaith coalition, public protests and delegation at 2003 Accra talks.

sources.title: Nobel Prize: 2011 Peace Prize press release
sources.note: Award to Ellen Johnson Sirleaf, Leymah Gbowee and Yemen’s Tawakkul Karman; women’s participation and nonviolent peace work.

sources.title: United Nations Peacekeeping: UNMIL completes its mandate
sources.note: 30 March 2018 closure announcement; mission following 2003 Comprehensive Peace Agreement.

sources.title: UNICEF: Heroes Wash Their Hands
sources.note: 23 October 2025 account of 15 October D. Tweh Memorial School event and Zwedru activities; avoid inconsistent household percentages.
